expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides domain types (ids.ts, money.ts, refund.ts), config, service (refund-service.ts), HTTP handler (post-refunds.ts), Prisma schema additions, two migration files, and test suite—all inline

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: RefundCommand schema has `idempotencyKey: IdempotencyKey` (no .optional()); HTTP handler returns 400 if header missing: `if (!key.success) { res.status(400)...return; }`

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: Schema declares `@@unique([orderId, idempotencyKey])`; migration creates index `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Refund_orderId_idempotencyKey_key"`; application logic (replay function) handles violations but database enforces the constraint

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: ids.ts defines `OrderId = z.string().uuid().brand<"OrderId">()` and `RefundId = z.string().uuid().brand<"RefundId">()` as distinct branded types

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
expectations.evidence: Cents = z.number().int().positive().max(MAX_REFUND_CENTS); all amounts use Cents type throughout service

expectations.text: Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Transaction uses guarded UPDATE: `UPDATE "Order" ... WHERE ... AND "refundedCents" + ${cmd.amountCents} <= "totalCents"` with check `if (rows !== 1) throw new OverRefund()`

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: Uses compound unique `id_tenantId` for order lookup; refund includes `tenantId: session.data.tenantId` (never from body); foreign key includes tenantId: `(orderId, tenantId, currency)`

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 'What rung each device reached' lists 8 misuses (cross-tenant refund, duplicate refund on retry, over-refund race, etc.) with specific devices and rungs

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Section 'What I consciously left possible' names 4 things: stranded PENDING refunds (needs reconciler), illegal transitions in app only, zero-decimal currency error, and partial refund currency mismatch
